concepts.name: JDK, JRE and JVM roles
concepts.summary: Explain that the JDK provides tools like javac, the JRE provides what is needed to run programs, and the JVM executes bytecode.

concepts.name: Primitive and reference types
concepts.summary: Distinguish primitives such as int and boolean from reference types such as String and understand that variable types are fixed at compile time.

concepts.name: Class structure and main method
concepts.summary: Recall how a class is declared in a file of the same name and how main serves as the program entry point.

concepts.name: Compile and run cycle
concepts.summary: Describe how javac turns .java source into .class bytecode that the java launcher runs on a JVM.

concepts.name: Objects and constructors
concepts.summary: Understand that a class is a blueprint, and new calls a constructor to create an object with its own fields.

concepts.name: Methods, fields and access modifiers
concepts.summary: Understand how instance members hold state and behaviour and how public and private control visibility.

concepts.name: Compiler error reading
concepts.summary: Interpret common javac messages such as missing symbol or incompatible types to locate the cause.

misconceptions.text: Java source code is run directly by the computer's processor after compiling.
The JVM and the JDK are the same thing.
Assigning one object variable to another copies the object itself.

concepts.name: Inheritance and method overriding
concepts.summary: Use extends, super and @Override to specialise a class and reuse behaviour from a superclass.

concepts.name: Interfaces and implementation
concepts.summary: Define an interface and implement it in classes, programming against the interface type.

concepts.name: Abstract classes
concepts.summary: Use abstract classes to share partial implementation while forcing subclasses to supply abstract methods.

concepts.name: Polymorphism and dynamic dispatch
concepts.summary: Apply a supertype reference to hold subclass objects and predict which overridden method runs.

concepts.name: ArrayList usage
concepts.summary: Add, get, remove and iterate over an ArrayList, including with the enhanced for loop.

concepts.name: Equals and hashCode contract
concepts.summary: Use equals to compare content instead of ==, and see why equal objects need equal hash codes in HashMap keys.

concepts.name: HashMap usage
concepts.summary: Store, look up and iterate key-value pairs in a HashMap and handle missing keys.

concepts.name: Try-catch and checked exceptions
concepts.summary: Handle or declare checked exceptions with try, catch, finally and throws.

misconceptions.text: Using == on two Strings or objects compares their contents.
A class can extend several classes as long as it is careful.
The method that runs is chosen by the declared type of the variable rather than the actual object.

concepts.name: Generic classes and methods
concepts.summary: Write and use generic types and methods so type errors are caught at compile time without casts.

concepts.name: Bounded types and wildcards
concepts.summary: Analyse when to use bounded type parameters and ? extends or ? super wildcards for flexible APIs.

concepts.name: Lambdas and functional interfaces
concepts.summary: Write lambdas and method references that target functional interfaces such as Predicate and Function.

concepts.name: Stream pipelines
concepts.summary: Decompose data processing into source, intermediate operations and a terminal operation, including collectors like groupingBy.

concepts.name: Collections framework selection
concepts.summary: Choose between ArrayList, LinkedList, HashSet, TreeMap and others based on ordering, uniqueness and performance.

concepts.name: Custom and unchecked exceptions
concepts.summary: Distinguish checked from unchecked exceptions and design custom exceptions with try-with-resources for cleanup.

concepts.name: Maven or Gradle project builds
concepts.summary: Use a build tool to declare dependencies, run the build lifecycle and tests, and package a JAR.

concepts.name: Immutability and Optional
concepts.summary: Analyse how immutable classes and Optional reduce null-related errors and shared-state bugs.

misconceptions.text: A List<Dog> can be passed where a List<Animal> is expected because Dog extends Animal.
Streams store data like a collection and can be reused after a terminal operation.
Generic type information is fully available at runtime.

concepts.name: Type erasure consequences
concepts.summary: Analyse how erasure limits generic arrays, instanceof checks and overloads, and why bridge methods and unchecked warnings appear.

concepts.name: Class loading and bytecode structure
concepts.summary: Analyse how class loaders load, link and initialise classes and read bytecode with javap to explain behaviour.

concepts.name: Garbage collection and memory model
concepts.summary: Reason about heap versus stack, object reachability, and how collector choice and allocation patterns affect latency and throughput.

concepts.name: API and class design tradeoffs
concepts.summary: Evaluate choices between inheritance, composition, interfaces with default methods and sealed hierarchies.

concepts.name: Concurrency primitives and visibility
concepts.summary: Analyse race conditions and visibility problems and apply synchronized, volatile, atomics and concurrent collections.

concepts.name: Stream performance and parallelism
concepts.summary: Evaluate when sequential, parallel or plain loop approaches are appropriate given statefulness, side effects and workload.

concepts.name: Multi-module dependency management
concepts.summary: Evaluate dependency scopes, transitive conflicts and version management in multi-module Maven or Gradle builds.

concepts.name: Profiling and diagnosing performance
concepts.summary: Use profilers, thread dumps and heap dumps to find the cause of slowness, leaks and deadlocks.

misconceptions.text: Parallel streams always make processing faster.
Garbage collection means memory leaks are impossible in Java.
Synchronizing every method makes a class thread-safe and efficient.

concepts.name: JIT compilation and optimisation
concepts.summary: Evaluate how JIT inlining, escape analysis and warm-up shape performance and the validity of benchmarks.

concepts.name: Java Memory Model happens-before
concepts.summary: Judge the correctness of concurrent code by reasoning with happens-before rules, safe publication and reordering.

concepts.name: Microbenchmark design
concepts.summary: Assess and design benchmarks that avoid dead-code elimination, constant folding and warm-up artefacts.

concepts.name: Designing library and framework APIs
concepts.summary: Create APIs that remain binary and source compatible, using generics, interfaces, sealed types and modules deliberately.

concepts.name: Bytecode manipulation and reflection
concepts.summary: Design solutions using reflection, annotation processors, proxies or agents, weighing their cost and safety.

concepts.name: Concurrency architecture choices
concepts.summary: Design concurrent systems choosing among platform threads, virtual threads, executors and async composition for a workload.

concepts.name: Reproducible build and release engineering
concepts.summary: Create reproducible, cached builds with custom plugins, versioning and release pipelines across large codebases.

concepts.name: JVM tuning and production diagnostics
concepts.summary: Evaluate GC selection and JVM flag settings against production metrics and justify tuning decisions.

misconceptions.text: Java benchmark results from a single short run reflect steady-state performance.
Tuning JVM flags is a reliable substitute for fixing allocation or design problems.
Virtual threads speed up CPU-bound work.
